chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The gatherings are with confidentiality, and no one should narrate a saying that its owner wishes to keep secret, except with his permission, unless he is trustworthy or does so to mention him in a good light.

key_terms.ذِكْراً لَهُ بِخَيْرٍ: mentioning him in a good light/praise

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on sharing a friend's private conversation with others?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the sanctity of trust (amanah) in social interactions, establishing that private discourse remains confidential unless the speaker grants permission for its dissemination. It introduces a nuanced exception for those known for trustworthiness (thiqah) or those intending to convey praise (dhikran lihi bi-khayr), reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving dignity while allowing beneficial communication. This principle serves as a foundational ethical guideline for maintaining social harmony and preventing gossip (ghibah) within the community.

en.hubeali:
A nuuumber of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The gatherings are with the confidentiality. No one must make public anything that one’s companion does not want to be made public unless it with his permission, or he is trusted and does it only for his good’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from those whom he has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The meetings are trusts. No one must make public anything that one’s companion does not want to be made public unless it is with his permission, or he is trusted and does it only for his good.”
